name: Conscript Helm
description: A battered iron helm worn by new recruits.

name: Conscript Collar
description: A crude neck guard offering minimal protection.

name: Conscript Chest
description: Padded leather chest armour. Stops the smallest of blows.

name: Iron Ring
description: A plain iron ring. Somehow sharpens the wearer's strikes.

name: Worn Band
description: A scratched metal band. No discernible power remains.

name: Draft Horse
description: A sturdy workhorse. Occasionally charges into the fray with surprising force.

name: Conscript Boots
description: Worn leather boots. Better than bare feet.

name: Conscript Gloves
description: Rough cloth gloves. Barely break-in.

name: Pano's War Helm
description: Legendary questing helm of the lost vanguard Pano. Hums with old power.

name: Pano's Amulet
description: An amulet warm to the touch, part of Pano's questing regalia.

name: Pano's Cuirass
description: The famed breastplate of Pano. Turns aside blows that would fell a lesser fighter.

name: Pano's Signet
description: A signet ring that sharpens the wearer's strikes.

name: Pano's Band
description: The companion band to Pano's signet. Steadies the hand in battle.

name: Pano's Steed
description: Pano's tireless warhorse. Charges with devastating force.

name: Pano's Greaves
description: Greaves that carry the wearer surefooted across any field.

name: Pano's Gauntlets
description: Gauntlets that lend crushing strength to every strike.

name: Oathsteel Helm
description: Forged from oathsteel and the shards of a hundred conscript helms.

name: Weir Kettle Helm
description: Frontier issue. The brim is wide because rain ruins a bowstring faster than an enemy does.

name: Weir Gorget
description: Plate at the throat and nowhere else. The Weir learned which wounds end a watch.

name: Weir Brigandine
description: Riveted from the scrap of three older coats. Every plate in it has already survived something.

name: Causeway Seal Ring
description: Ash-pitted signet of a road warden. The Ashen Causeway still has wardens. They are just not paid.

name: Marchwarden's Band
description: Worn thin at one edge, where a thumb rubbed through forty years of standing still.

name: Weir Courser
description: Bred for the courier roads. Not fast. Tireless, which on the frontier is the same as fast.

name: Weir Marchboots
description: Resoled more times than made. The Weir counts a boot's age in roads, not years.

name: Weir Handguards
description: Cut long at the wrist. A frontier warden reaches into places they cannot see.

name: Relaykeeper's Hood
description: Oiled against frost, hemmed in lamp-black. Worn by the ones who kept the dead lamps burning.

name: Torc of the Quiet Wind
description: Cold iron, warm at the throat. The Watch says it hums a half-beat before a relay fails.

name: Relay Coat
description: Long, grey, unremarkable, which is the point. A courier who is looked at twice is a dead courier.

name: Lamplighter's Seal
description: Proof the bearer may enter a sealed relay. Nine in ten of those relays no longer answer.

name: Vaultkeeper's Band
description: Taken from the Sunken Vaults, which the Watch marked as sealed and the water did not.

name: Relay Charger
description: Trained to run a route with no rider. Several still do, on roads no one has walked in an Age.

name: Frostmere Treads
description: Nailed for ice. Frostmere takes a careless step and keeps it.

name: Lampwright's Grips
description: Scorched across the palms. The lamps of the Watch were never meant to be handled cold.

name: Sable Vein Circlet
description: Archive work. The script around the band is a catalogue number, and the thing catalogued is you.

name: Threnody Collar
description: Worn by a scribe who recorded a Manifestation from close enough to be corrected by it.

name: Mantle of the Sable Vein
description: Black on black, and the inner black is older. The Houses do not explain their dyes.

name: House Sable Seal
description: Opens an archive hall that appears on no map the Houses admit to holding.

name: Vein-Cut Band
description: Split by a hairline fracture that has not widened in two hundred years of being watched.

name: Sable Courser
description: Archive stock. It will not cross running water, and the Houses have never said why.

name: Stair-Worn Boots
description: Taken off the Eternal Stair. The wear is at the toe, not the heel. Whoever wore them was climbing.

name: Archivist's Grips
description: Thin, precise, reinforced at the fingertips. Some things in an archive must be held down.

name: The Cinder-Cuff
description: Wrath-slag, cooled and cuffed. It makes the wearer stronger and angrier in the same motion, and does not distinguish between the two.

name: The Unworn Crown
description: A circlet of a dark metal no living smith can name, made for a head no carving depicts. It has never, in any account, been worn. The Old Guard kept it because they were afraid to be the ones who found out why.

name: The Vanguard's Cold Token
description: Kin to the lost signet: the same unknown script worn nearly smooth, the same cold that does not warm in the hand. Nobody alive can read it. That is the whole of what is known.

name: Colossus-Core Shard
description: Pried from a war-construct that never stood down. It still pulses with the last order it was given, and there is no one left to amend it: hold.

name: Sovereign's Tithe-Mark
description: Granted by the Gauntlet in the name of the founding pact. It marks a fighter as having paid the tithe. What the Sovereign was promised is recorded nowhere a fighter may read.

name: The Sealwright's Stylus
description: The instrument that inscribed null-sigil bindings, the script that holds a thing closed. The Old Guard made few and accounted for every one. This one is not on the ledger.

name: Warrens Lamp-Hood
description: A hood with a lamp bracket sewn at the temple. Both hands stay free, which in a warren is the whole argument.

name: Ratter's Choker
description: Leather, doubled. Goblins go for the throat because it works, so the Weir stopped leaving it bare.

name: Warrens Jack
description: Quilted and short-cut. Long coats catch on everything down there, and everything down there catches back.

name: Tunnel-Warden's Seal
description: Marks the bearer as the one who counts everyone back out. It is not a promotion.

name: Knuckle-Ring of the Weir
description: Worn on the outside of the glove. Frontier smiths call this an ornament and frontier wardens do not.

name: Warrens Pit-Pony
description: Small, foul-tempered, and unbothered by the dark. It has walked out of places its riders did not.

name: Warrens Treads
description: Nailed flat for wet stone. A warren floor is never dry and never once been level.

name: Ratter's Grips
description: Reinforced across the back of the hand. You will be hitting things that are already biting you.

name: Marchwatch Helm
description: Open-faced, because a watch that cannot see is a wall with a man behind it.

name: Watchman's Gorget
description: Plain steel, no device. A marchwatch is not a house and does not want to be mistaken for one.

name: Long Marchwatch Coat
description: Cut to the knee and lined against the wind. Most of the job is weather.

name: Ring of the Standing Watch
description: Given at the end of a first full winter on the line. Most are given posthumously; this one was not.

name: Tally-Ring
description: Notched once a season. A warden with a smooth ring is new; one with a worn ring is rare.

name: Marchwatch Rounder
description: Trained to walk a circuit and stop at every marker without being asked. It knows the route better than the rider.

name: Marchwatch Boots
description: Heavy, and worn through at the heel rather than the toe — the wear pattern of a man who stands.

name: Watch Mitts
description: Split at the fingertips so a bowstring can still be felt. Frostbite is a slower enemy but it is patient.

name: Gravewarden's Hood
description: Waxed against the smell. The Watch is direct about what the job involves.

name: Seal of the Quiet Ground
description: Worn so a warden can be identified if they do not come back up. It has been needed.

name: Gravewarden's Coat
description: Heavy canvas with iron at the forearms, because the thing you are moving sometimes moves back.

name: Binding Band
description: Old sigil-work, worn smooth. It does not hold anything closed any more. The Watch wears it anyway.

name: Warden's Signet
description: Authorises the bearer to open a marked grave. There is no ring that authorises closing one.

name: Gravewarden's Dray
description: Bred to stand still while unpleasant work happens behind it. The rarest quality a horse can have.

name: Marsh Wades
description: Thigh-high and pitch-sealed. The Hollow Marches are where the Watch does most of this.

name: Gravewarden's Gauntlets
description: Iron over leather over iron. Whatever is down there does not get to hold your hand.

name: Salvager's Helm
description: Sealed at the collar with a glass plate. The Vaults are dark before they are deep.

name: Tidewatch Torc
description: Cold in cold water, warm in water that is not. Salvagers do not agree on what the warm kind means.

name: Salvage Harness
description: Rings and line, no plate. Down there weight is not protection, it is a decision.

name: Vault-Seal Ring
description: Old Guard work. It opens one door in the Sunken Vaults and nobody has found which.

name: Barnacle Band
description: Recovered encrusted and left that way. Coast salvagers say a clean ring means a short career.

name: Coastwise Courser
description: Sure-footed on wet shale and entirely unwilling to enter water above the knee. It has its reasons.

name: Shalewalkers
description: Soled in cork and iron. The Drowned Coast is loose all the way down.

name: Salvager's Grips
description: Webbed, tarred, and cut short at the thumb so a knot can still be tied blind.

name: Breaker's Visor
description: Slit-narrow and backed in lead. A Wrought does not aim, which makes it worse, not better.

name: Siege Collar
description: Braced to the shoulders. It exists so the head stays on when the arm stops something heavy.

name: Wroughtbreaker Plate
description: Layered against impact rather than edge. Nothing made by the Old Guard bothers with edges.

name: Sigil-Key Ring
description: Reads a commanding sigil well enough to guess at its order. Guessing is the whole trade.

name: Breaker's Band
description: Cast from the melt of a construct that finally stopped. The Weir keeps the melt and the tally.

name: Siege Destrier
description: Trained to stand under a falling thing. Horses are not built for this and it is taught anyway.

name: Breaker's Sabatons
description: Weighted so a shove does not become a fall. A Wrought's first move is almost always a shove.

name: Wroughtbreaker Gauntlets
description: Built to hold a bar against a moving core until the order stops. Most pairs are used once.

name: Listener's Circlet
description: Thin, and open at the ears by design. The Choir does not cover what it uses.

name: Resonant Stole
description: It hums a half-tone under any sung note. The Choir considers this agreement.

name: Dawnward Vestment
description: Undyed, unadorned, and cut so it hangs still in wind. Movement is noise and noise is interference.

name: Ring of the First Answer
description: Worn by whoever spoke when something answered. The Choir has four. It will not say to what.

name: Attendant's Band
description: Given to those who stand and do not sing. Somebody has to be listening to the listeners.

name: Choir Palfrey
description: Trained to a whisper and unshod, so a procession arrives without announcing itself.

name: Vigil Slippers
description: Soft-soled. The Choir keeps its vigils barefoot where the ground permits and these where it does not.

name: Cantor's Wraps
description: Linen, wound to the second knuckle. A Cantor's hands are for counting time, not for holding.

name: Sovereign's Diadem
description: Worn by whoever currently holds the Dragon bracket. It is returned, always, and never willingly.

name: Collar of the Founding Pact
description: Names the Gauntlet's first tithe in a script the tournament no longer teaches.

name: Regalia Cuirass
description: Ceremonial in cut and emphatically not in construction. The Gauntlet has always been honest about that.

name: Sovereign's Signet
description: Opens the Gauntlet's inner registry. What is written there is the pact's other half.

name: Tithe-Band
description: One notch per climb paid. Nobody has found the ring where the notches run out.

name: Sovereign's Wyrm
description: Not a gift. A loan, from an institution that has never once explained its terms.

name: Regalia Greaves
description: Made to be seen on a stair. The Eternal Stair, specifically, and the Gauntlet knows it.

name: Sovereign's Gauntlets
description: The Gauntlet's namesake, and the only pair the tournament has ever formally issued.

name: The Sundown Ember
description: Rolled at dusk, lit at dusk, and worn behind one ear like a circlet by an archdevil who maintains this is what it is for. The congregation stopped correcting him some centuries ago. It has never gone out, and nobody has ever seen him relight it.

name: The Perpetual Censer
description: A vessel lit some time during the Age of Dawn and never once refilled. There is still some left. There has always been some left. Those who come to kneel do not always remember, afterwards, what they came to ask.

name: Robe of the Long Sabbatical
description: Cut for a being who intended to sit down and has now been sitting down for an Age. Remarkably comfortable. Alarmingly hard to damage. It smells, faintly and permanently, of the room.

name: Signet of Declined Ascendancy
description: He was offered a throne. He read the terms, asked two questions nobody could answer, and went back inside. He says he will look at it again. He has been saying so for four hundred years.

name: Band of the Fourth Reconsideration
description: There were three earlier ones. He is not looking for them. He is fairly certain one of them is in the garden.

name: Extremely Relaxed Hell-Goat
description: It will carry you anywhere at exactly one speed. Attempts to hurry it have never once succeeded and, by every account, have never once been forgiven.

name: Slippers of the Unwalked Path
description: Immaculate. Not a scuff on them. He means to go out. He means to go out most evenings.

name: Mitts of Amiable Menace
description: He shakes hands. It is worse than the alternative and takes considerably longer. He will ask after your family, and he will remember the answer, which is the genuinely frightening part.

name: Iron Shard
description: A fragment of the Iron Colossus. Used in crafting.

name: Arcane Dust
description: Residual arcane energy left behind by Malachar's servants.

name: Minor Stat Bag
description: Contains 5 unassigned skill points. Use to add to your stat pool.

name: Major Stat Bag
description: Contains 15 unassigned skill points. Use to add to your stat pool.

name: Minor Energy Draught
description: Restores 25 Energy. The road does not walk itself.

name: Energy Draught
description: Restores 60 Energy. Brewed for those who refuse to stop.

name: Minor Stamina Draught
description: Restores 25 Stamina. Steadies the arm for one more strike.

name: Stamina Draught
description: Restores 60 Stamina. The long fight favours the prepared.

name: Minor Healing Poultice
description: Restores 25 Health. Crude, bitter, and enough.

name: Healing Poultice
description: Restores 60 Health. Closes what the raid opened.

name: Ancient's Restorative
description: Refills your Energy completely. Found, never sold.

name: Oathsteel Ingot
description: Steel quenched in a spoken oath. The forge remembers what was promised.

name: Vanguard Banner
description: Carried at the front until the front moved. Proof of a line that held.

name: Wyrm Scale
description: Prised from a raid boss that did not part with it willingly.

name: Causeway Ash
description: Grey, weightless, and everywhere on the Ashen Causeway. Smiths pack it around a quench because it takes heat without ever giving it back.

name: Hollow Marches Reed
description: Grows only where the ground is too wet to bury anything. The Marches are full of them.

name: Emberfall Slag
description: Run-off from a fire that burned in the Age of Dawn and has not entirely stopped. Warm at the core a thousand years after the fact.

name: Keepwall Mortar
description: Prised from a wall Malachar's masons raised in one night. Nobody has explained the speed.

name: Rime-Glass
description: Frostmere water frozen so slowly it set clear. It does not melt in the hand. It does not melt in a forge either, which is the difficulty.

name: Cinder-Salt
description: Scraped off the Ashen Throne, where the heat drove everything out of the stone but this. Tastes of iron. Nobody tastes it twice.

name: Star Hollow Dust
description: Collected where the sky is closest and least reliable. It settles upward if left alone, so it is never left alone.

name: Mire-Ichor
description: Pale, luminous, foul. Bled from the Brood-things of the drowned shallows. Useless alone; the basis of half the alchemy on the Drowned Coast.

name: Mire-Brood Chitin
description: Plate from a thing that grows a new one each season and abandons the old where it stood.

name: Ashen Stag Heart-Tendon
description: The Heartmarch hunters string bows with it and say an arrow loosed from one arrives before the sound does.

name: Wrath-Slag
description: The cooled residue of a Manifestation. Still faintly warm an Age later, and still, very slightly, trying to qualify whoever holds it.

name: Leviathan Baleen
description: Cut from a Primordial that was never killed, only out-waited. It filters things out of air that air was not known to contain.

name: Colossus Filament
description: Sigil-wire from the Iron Colossus's commanding core. Still carrying an order. Still trying to deliver it to a chain of command four hundred years dead.

name: Sounding-Horn of the Sunken Leviathan
description: It still holds one note. The Old Guard who took it never agreed on what the note does, only that the sea answered the one time it was sounded.

name: Haft of Gravewend
description: A farm tool from a village whose name is not written down, carried by a man whose name is not written down, who used it to kill a thing that should have killed him. The village is gone. The pitchfork is not.

name: Null-Sigil Ink
description: The medium the Sealwrights wrote closure in. It does not dry so much as decide to stop.

name: Quiet Lamp Oil
description: Drawn from a Last Watch relay lamp that has burned unattended since the fall. The Watch does not know what it burns and has stopped asking.

name: Greater Energy Draught
description: Restores 150 Energy. Brewed at the relays, for a road that does not end at dusk.

name: Grand Energy Draught
description: Restores 400 Energy. The Weir issues these to couriers who are not expected back soon.

name: Greater Stamina Draught
description: Restores 150 Stamina. The arm gives out before the will does. This is for the arm.

name: Grand Stamina Draught
description: Restores 400 Stamina. Drunk before a company commits to something it cannot walk away from.

name: Greater Healing Poultice
description: Restores 150 Health. Closes what a company opened.

name: Ancient's Draught
description: Refills your Stamina completely. Found, never sold.

name: Greater Stat Bag
description: Contains 40 unassigned skill points. Old Guard requisition, unopened since the fall.

name: Ancient's Reliquary
description: Contains 100 unassigned skill points. What the Dawnward Choir calls an answer.

name: Sigil of the Last Lamp
description: The name of a lamp that has not gone out. Speak it and the vigil resumes.

name: Sigil of the Last Lamp (Hard)
description: The name of a lamp that has not gone out. Spoken harder, it answers harder.

name: Sigil of the Last Lamp (Legendary)
description: The name of a lamp that has not gone out, and of the thing that has been circling it.

name: Sigil of the Last Lamp (Nightmare)
description: The name of a lamp that has not gone out. At this pitch, something else uses the name too.

name: Warren Teeth
description: Goblins replace them constantly and leave the old ones where they fall. A tunnel floor is half gravel and half this.

name: Brood Carapace
description: Plate off something that outgrew three of these before anyone got close enough to measure.

name: Ashen Stag Ash
description: What is left where one lay down. The Heartmarch hunters do not collect it and will not say why.

name: Deepwood Heart
description: Cut from an apex that had been growing since before the Sundering. Still warm four days out.

name: Gravesalt
description: The Watch packs it around anything it has to move twice. It works, and nobody has asked how.

name: Barrow Iron
description: Grave-goods iron, buried long enough to take on the habit. It does not rust and it does not hold an edge — the Watch considers the trade fair.

name: Amber Rot
description: The Awakening's own residue. It is warm, it is slightly wrong, and it keeps indefinitely in a sealed jar that nobody wants in their pack.

name: Glutbound Core
description: The dense part of a thing that had nearly finished becoming something else.

name: Cracked Command Sigil
description: Prised off a Wrought mid-order. It is still trying to finish the sentence.

name: Brimstone Slag
description: Cools where a Swollen thing stood too long. Emberpan is paved in it, mostly.

name: Leviathan Tooth
description: One of very many, and still the largest object most people will ever hold.

name: Kronarch's Broken Seal
description: From the muster-rolls of the army that won against nothing. Most of the names are legible.

name: Sovereign's Shed Scale
description: The Gauntlet collects them. It has never said what for and has never been asked twice.

name: Lamp-Black
description: Soot off a relay lamp, ground fine. The Watch hems its hoods with it so a courier does not shine in a doorway.

name: Sable Vein Thread
description: The Houses dye it twice and will not discuss the second dye.

name: Marsh Pitch
description: Boiled down over three days. Gravewardens seal their wades with it and their coffins too.

name: Cork-and-Iron Sole
description: Salvager's stock. Buoyant enough to float a boot and heavy enough to keep it down.

name: Resonant Brass
description: Cast to hum at one note and no other. The Choir orders it by the tone, never the weight.

name: Siege Lead
description: Backing for a breaker's visor. A Wrought does not aim, which makes shielding a guess everywhere at once.

name: Relay Draught
description: Restores 900 Energy. Issued to a courier who is not expected to stop.

name: Warhorn Draught
description: Restores 900 Stamina. Drunk by a company that has decided the thing in front of it is going down today.

name: Grand Healing Poultice
description: Restores 400 Health. Field-standard for anything the Weir calls a bad week.

name: Ancient's Mending
description: Refills your Health completely. Found, never sold.

name: Oathsworn Cache
description: Contains 65 unassigned skill points. Left by a company that did not need them after all.

name: The Devil's Tea
description: Restores 260 Energy. He offers it to everyone who comes to kill him. Several have stayed for a second cup and one is reportedly still there.

name: The Long Afternoon
description: Restores 260 Stamina. Bottled from a nap of genuinely historic proportions.

name: Perpetual Censer Resin
description: Scraped from the inside of a censer lit during the Age of Dawn. There is still some left. There has always been some left.

name: Unwalked Leather
description: Cut for slippers that were never worn outdoors. Immaculate, and faintly reproachful.

name: A Moment's Reconsideration
description: Grants 25 unassigned skill points. He suggests you think about where you put them. He is not going to elaborate and he is not going to stop looking at you.

name: Bog Cotton
description: Grows in standing water and pulls out in handfuls. Wadding, tinder, bandage — a Weir pack carries it because it is the cheapest thing that is ever useful.

name: Road Flint
description: Picked off any causeway by anyone who bothers to look down. It has started every fire the frontier has ever needed and it has never once been remarkable.

name: Rendered Tallow
description: Every relay lamp in the Watch burns it, every boot in the Weir is greased with it, and nobody has ever written a sentence about it before this one.

name: Coarse Thread
description: Spun thick enough to sew canvas and cheap enough to waste. The frontier repairs more than it replaces, and this is what it repairs with.

name: Whetstone
description: Sharpens every blow; a guaranteed small bonus on every hit.

name: Lesser Poison
description: A weak venom that occasionally laces attacks.

name: Poison
description: A reliable venom that procs with moderate frequency.

name: Greater Poison
description: A potent venom with meaningful proc damage.

name: Smite
description: The pinnacle strike. It lands often enough that you plan around it.

name: Blessing of Might
description: The pinnacle boon. Sustained, reliable, and never a gamble.

name: Impending Doom
description: A catastrophic curse that rarely fires but devastates when it does.

name: Expose Weakness
description: Reveals a flaw in the target's defence, increasing crit chance.

name: Midas Touch
description: Every hit has a chance to yield bonus gold.

name: Kindling
description: Occasionally doubles the experience earned from a hit.

name: Luminary's Echo
description: PLACEHOLDER. A pinnacle magic awarded at level 5,000. Its entire effect — proc, drop, or something stranger — is designed by the first player to reach this level; everyone who arrives afterwards receives that design and keeps it. Inert until then.

name: Archon's Decree
description: PLACEHOLDER. A pinnacle magic awarded at level 7,500. Its entire effect — proc, drop, or something stranger — is designed by the first player to reach this level; everyone who arrives afterwards receives that design and keeps it. Inert until then.

name: Ancient's Wrath
description: PLACEHOLDER. A pinnacle magic awarded at level 10,000. Its entire effect — proc, drop, or something stranger — is designed by the first player to reach this level; everyone who arrives afterwards receives that design and keeps it. Inert until then.

name: Elder Resonance
description: PLACEHOLDER. A pinnacle magic awarded at level 15,000. Its entire effect — proc, drop, or something stranger — is designed by the first player to reach this level; everyone who arrives afterwards receives that design and keeps it. Inert until then.

name: Eternal Aspect
description: PLACEHOLDER. A pinnacle magic awarded at level 25,000. Its entire effect — proc, drop, or something stranger — is designed by the first player to reach this level; everyone who arrives afterwards receives that design and keeps it. Inert until then.

name: Wrath of the Ancients
description: The Gauntlet rank-1 aura. An off-cap proc applied to the Gauntlet raid, outside the five-magic slot cap. Rank-acquired only (per-event consumable).

name: Blessing of the Ancients
description: The Gauntlet ranks 2–10 aura. An off-cap proc applied to the Gauntlet raid, outside the five-magic slot cap. Rank-acquired only (per-event consumable).

name: Hollow Point
description: A round bored out and left empty. What fills it on the way in is the argument.

name: Rimefang
description: Frostmere ice that never gave up being water. It finds the gap in a thing and then widens it.

name: Sunder
description: Old Guard siege doctrine, reduced to one word and one motion.

name: Wrathslag Ember
description: A coal off a Manifestation. Still warm, still trying, still not quite a Herald.

name: Kronarch's Last Order
description: The command he gave when the tide went out and nothing answered. It still lands.

name: Keen Eye
description: The Watch teaches it before it teaches anything else: look at the seam, not the shield.

name: Reader's Mark
description: House Sable Vein trains a scribe to find the one line that matters. It transfers.

name: The Veiled Eye
description: Discernment's own nature, briefly lent. It does not see everything. It sees the thing that matters.

name: The Sealwright's Measure
description: Before you can close a thing you must know exactly where it opens.

name: Coin-Sense
description: A caravan lord's habit, distilled. It notices what a room is worth on the way in.

name: Tithe Ledger
description: The Gauntlet has kept one since its founding. Nobody has audited it and nobody has offered.

name: Hoarder's Eye
description: Hoard's dominion is not petty. It is the principle of accumulation itself, and it is contagious.

name: Spoils of the March
description: What an army leaves is worth more than what it carried. The Weir has always known this.

name: The Sovereign's Cut
description: Every climb pays a tithe. This is the arrangement that decides which way it flows.

name: Drillmaster's Cant
description: The Weir's marching count. Nothing about it is magical and it works anyway.

name: Field Commission
description: Promotion granted where it was earned, by whoever was still standing to grant it.

name: The Long Watch
description: Four hundred years of standing somewhere, compressed into the part that teaches.

name: Fragment of the Age of Dawn
description: A piece of a lesson from before the Sundering. The rest of it is not recoverable.

name: Steady Hand
description: Never misses, never surprises. The Weir issues it to anyone who has been startled once too often.

name: Gambler's Sigil
description: Old Guard camp-work, technically forbidden. Enforcement was reportedly inconsistent.

name: Wardens' Metronome
description: It keeps time, and every beat lands. Small, certain, endless.

name: Wick of the Last Lamp
description: It burns very slowly and it has never gone out. Arveth's lamp is still lit on the same principle.

name: The One True Swing
description: Gravewend's peasant got exactly one. The pitchfork remembers the shape of it — and has learned to repeat it.

name: Considered Inaction
description: The archdevil's contribution to the war effort. He thought about it for an Age and then, on balance, contributed this. It is genuinely quite good, which nobody has forgiven.

name: Luminary's Vow
description: PLACEHOLDER. A pinnacle magic awarded at level 2,500. Its entire effect — proc, drop, or something stranger — is designed by the first player to reach this level; everyone who arrives afterwards receives that design and keeps it. Inert until then.

name: Ascendant's Banner
description: The first standard planted past the thousandth mark. It does not make its bearer stronger so much as it makes everyone within sight of it harder to discourage — and the less a soldier brought to the field, the more the banner gives back. Adds a flat +120 Attack to every blow struck against this raid, by anyone, for as long as it stands.

name: Ironward the Steadfast
description: A stalwart Human Tank general whose shield stance can deflect devastating strikes.

name: Ashblade
description: A swift Human Melee general who strikes with burning precision.

name: Sylvaire
description: An Elf Ranged general whose arrows seek vital points with unerring accuracy.

name: Morvath the Unliving
description: An Undead Special general whose cursed wisdom amplifies every strike of his legion.

name: Conscript Militia
description: Untrained Human foot soldiers — numerous but unremarkable.

name: Wood Archers
description: Elf Ranged troops who pepper enemies from a distance.

name: Iron Pikemen
description: Stalwart Human Tank troops who hold the line against any charge.

name: Shadow Acolytes
description: Undead Special troops channeling dark wisdom into devastating blasts.

name: Ironward the Unbroken
description: Ironward reforged. The shield that deflected a wyrm now turns aside armies.

name: Ashblade, Emberborn
description: The blade drank the pyre and came back hungrier.

name: Oathsteel Pikemen
description: Iron pikes re-forged in oathsteel; the line does not break.

name: Gorruk Stonejaw
description: An Oroc line-holder who has never once been moved off a position he agreed to hold. The agreeing is the hard part.

name: Makh the Unhurried
description: Fights at exactly one speed. Opponents consistently mistake this for an opening.

name: Oroc Shieldline
description: They do not advance. That is not a limitation, it is the entire service being offered.

name: Oroc Maulers
description: Recruited by the Weir at rates it does not put in writing.

name: Durn Anvilkeep
description: Reads a construct's commanding sigil the way other people read weather. Wrong twice; he keeps both notes.

name: Brannoc Deepvein
description: The Weir's siege-master. Has taken down four Wrought and will discuss none of them.

name: Weir Sappers
description: They go under the thing. Frontier doctrine has never improved on this.

name: Anvilkeep Hammers
description: Issued one hammer and one instruction, both heavy.

name: The Ashen Stag
description: Not tamed. Accompanying. The Heartmarch hunters are precise about the distinction and have been since the first one tried the other word.

name: Mire-Brood Swarm
description: Bled for reagent, herded for war. Neither use was the Brood's idea.

name: Rimewood Wolves
description: They hunt the cold better than anything the Watch has ever fielded, and they know it.

name: Glacier-Maw Bears
description: Taken as cubs from a den nobody has found twice.

name: Sentinel Prime
description: Given a new order by someone with no authority to give it. It has not noticed, or it has and does not care, and the Weir has stopped asking which.

name: Salvaged Automata
description: Restarted, roughly. They execute the order and nothing else, including stopping.

name: Lamp-Walkers
description: Relay-work that kept walking its route after the relay fell. The Watch marches beside them now.

name: Vaskarr the Bargained
description: Bound by an agreement the Choir drafted and the Threnody Houses will not read aloud.

name: The Reconsidered
description: An archdevil's aide, sent along on the understanding that he would 'have a look'. He has had a look. He is still here. Nobody has raised it.

name: Emberpan Imps
description: Malicious, tireless, and extremely literal about instructions.

name: Slagborn
description: What cools where a Manifestation stood, if it cools into legs.

name: Sister Arveth of the Lamp
description: The lamp is named for her, not the other way round. She would like that corrected and the Watch has declined for two hundred years.

name: The Dawnward Choirmaster
description: Keeps a company standing by counting time at them. It should not work.

name: Field Chirurgeons
description: Weir-trained, which means fast, unsentimental, and usually right.

name: Choir Attendants
description: They stand and do not sing. Somebody has to be listening to the listeners.

name: Pano, the Lost Vanguard
description: The banner came back. Nobody has ever explained the rest of it, and the Watch has stopped asking in writing.

name: Vanguard Oathsworn
description: They swore to a man who did not come back, and have not considered that a release.

name: Sable Vein Witnesses
description: House scribes who record a fight from inside it. Their accounts are the only ones that agree.

name: Free Warband
description: An undisciplined but adaptable warband with no unit-type restrictions.

name: Dawn Vanguard
description: A disciplined vanguard formation with three general and three troop slots, open to any unit.

name: The Iron Legion
description: A specialist formation demanding Tank, Melee, and Ranged generals alongside Strength troops — its type-locked slots carry higher power bonus.

name: Dawn Vanguard II
description: The Vanguard rebuilt around a core of oathsteel — the same banner, twice the weight behind it.

name: The Houndsmen
description: A hunting company, not an army. Built around beasts and the people who can stand near them, it goes where a formation cannot and arrives sooner.

name: The Warrenguard
description: Iron Weir tunnel work. Short ranks, low ceilings, and a doctrine that assumes the enemy is already inside the line.

name: The Anvilkeep Siege
description: Dwarven engineers and the heaviest thing they could get to the site. It is slow, it is loud, and Wrought do not get back up.

name: The Bargained Company
description: Demons under written agreement, fielded by people who have read the agreement very carefully. It answers its own kind better than anything else will.

name: The Deepwatch
description: The Last Watch's answer to the things that were here first. Everyone in it has seen one and elected to come back, which is the only entry requirement.

name: The Sovereign's Climb
description: A Gauntlet formation, fielded under the founding pact. What it costs to raise is written in the inner registry, which fighters may not read.

name: Ironward the Unbroken
description: Reforge Ironward around a core of oathsteel. The general is consumed; what walks out is not the same man.

name: Ashblade, Emberborn
description: Quench Ashblade in wyrm-fire. Costly, and there is no way back to the blade you had.

name: Oathsteel Pikemen
description: Re-forge the pikes. The men are the same; the line no longer bends.

name: Dawn Vanguard II
description: Rebuild the Vanguard around a veteran core — the banner survives, the legion under it does not.

name: Oathsteel Helm
description: A hundred conscript helms, melted down and made to mean something.

name: Warrens Lamp-Hood
description: A hood, a bracket, and a lamp. The Weir has never improved on it and has stopped trying.

name: Long Marchwatch Coat
description: Cut to the knee and lined against the wind, because most of the job is weather.

name: A Warden's Measure of Gravesalt
description: The Watch packs it around anything it has to move twice. Six jars is a season.

name: Gravewarden's Coat
description: Heavy canvas with iron at the forearms, because the thing you are moving sometimes moves back.

name: Salvager's Helm
description: Sealed at the collar with a glass plate. The Vaults are dark before they are deep.

name: Breaker's Visor
description: Slit-narrow and backed in lead. A Wrought does not aim, which makes it worse, not better.

name: Resonant Stole
description: It hums a half-tone under any sung note. The Choir considers this agreement.

name: Wroughtbreaker Gauntlets
description: Built to hold a bar against a moving core until the order stops. Most pairs are used once.

name: Gravewarden's Gauntlets
description: Iron over leather over iron. Whatever is down there does not get to hold your hand.

name: Listener's Circlet
description: Thin, and open at the ears by design. The Choir does not cover what it uses.

name: Warrens Pit-Pony
description: Small, foul-tempered, and unbothered by the dark. Nobody has ever bred one on purpose twice.

name: Gravewarden's Dray
description: Bred to stand still while unpleasant work happens behind it. The rarest quality a horse can have.

name: Gorruk, Oathbound
description: The Oroc agreed to hold a position. Oathsteel is how the Weir makes an agreement heavier.

name: Durn, Sigil-Wise
description: He was wrong twice and kept both notes. This is what the notes were for.

name: Sovereign's Signet
description: Opens the Gauntlet's inner registry. What is written there is the pact's other half.

name: The Perpetual Censer
description: Lit some time during the Age of Dawn and never once since. Whatever is in it, there is still some left. The Choir has a theory. He has never confirmed or denied it and appears to find the question restful.

name: Slippers of the Unwalked Path
description: Immaculate. Not a scuff on them. Making a pair requires leather that has never been walked on, which is harder to source than it sounds and much harder to explain.

name: Extremely Relaxed Hell-Goat
description: It will carry you anywhere at exactly one speed. Attempts to hurry it have never once succeeded and, by every account, have never once been forgiven.

name: Guardian of the Throne of Ancients
